_metadata.independence: I read only u05-blind-input.json; no other file, search, web lookup or API was used.

hints.reason: Spider web is immediate, but APPLE reaches WEB only through Apple-the-tech-company and Safari, which is a thin route.
Taking a bite of an apple (Snow White, the Apple logo) and a spider bite (Spider-Man) are both everyday images.

best_available.why: Reaches both words through familiar images without any explanation.

pairs.pair_note: BITE is a clean, strong hint; WEB is essentially a spider hint with a weak Apple-company back door.

hints.reason: Apple orchard is a compound, but orchards reach SPRING only through the seasonal blooming association.
Apple blossom is a compound and blossom is the signature of spring.

best_available.why: A direct compound on one side and the defining image of the season on the other.

pairs.pair_note: BLOSSOM is excellent; ORCHARD is a weaker shadow of the same idea.

hints.reason: Apple seeds is plain, but the star-shaped seed pattern inside a sliced apple is trivia a player must already know, and SEEDS alone does not point at STAR.
Apple is a fruit and star fruit is a familiar compound; generic but it reaches both words.

best_available.why: Star fruit makes the STAR side concrete and the APPLE side is trivially true.

pairs.pair_note: FRUIT is the only hint that cleanly reaches STAR; SEEDS relies on a hidden-star fact that the hint itself does not signal.

hints.reason: Apple crate is a familiar object, but crates reach TRAIN only via generic freight hauling.
GRAND reaches TRAIN only through Grand Central and reaches APPLE only via the Apple Store inside that terminal, a two-step route no player would take.
Train station is immediate but there is no ordinary APPLE-station connection.

best_available.why: The only hint with a real foothold on both words, even though the TRAIN side is generic freight.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. GRAND and STATION both appear to lean on the Grand Central Apple Store, which is far too obscure for a one-word hint.

hints.reason: Apple juice is a compound, but WATER is reached only as a fellow drink or as something you dilute juice with.
Bobbing for apples is a game of apples floating in a tub of water, reaching both words through one shared scene.

best_available.why: One familiar Halloween scene that requires both apples and water.

pairs.pair_note: BOBBING is a model two-word hint; JUICE is mostly an apple hint.

hints.reason: Snow White's poisoned apple and the witch (the queen in hag disguise) who hands it over come from the same story.
Witch's broom is immediate, but BROOM has no ordinary route to APPLE.
The poisoned apple from the witch in Snow White reaches both words in one image, matching the POISON/APPLE+QUEEN anchor.

best_available.why: The poisoned apple is the single most famous witch-and-apple image.

pairs.pair_note: Two good Snow White routes; SNOW is slightly less direct because it names the victim rather than the act.

hints.reason: Wolves howl; nothing connects HOWL to APPLE.
Granny Smith apples on one side and the wolf disguised as Granny in Little Red Riding Hood on the other.

best_available.why: A brand-level apple variety and a famous story scene in one word.

pairs.pair_note: GRANNY is delightful; HOWL is pure filler.

hints.reason: Bat cave is immediate but CAVE has no ordinary route to BANK.
Blood bank is a compound and vampire bats drink blood.
Bats are nocturnal, but BANK is reached only through the night-deposit slot, which most players will not jump to.

best_available.why: Compound on one side, defining animal fact on the other.

pairs.pair_note: BLOOD is strong; NIGHT is a reasonable second but leans on bank jargon.

hints.reason: Both routes go through Wall Street (banks, bear markets), a two-step connection on each side.
Bears love honey; HONEY has no ordinary route to BANK.
Bear market is a set phrase and banks are the obvious players in financial markets.

best_available.why: Bear market is the one phrase that puts a bear in bank territory.

pairs.pair_note: MARKET is the only hint that reaches both; WALL is the same idea one hop further away.

hints.reason: Liberty Bell is famous, but the BANK side relies on regional Liberty Bank brands or the word on US coins.
A bank alarm during a robbery and an alarm bell are both everyday images.

best_available.why: Equally direct on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: ALARM carries the pair; LIBERTY is one-sided unless the player knows a Liberty Bank.

hints.reason: You cross a bridge, but reaching the far BANK is implied rather than said.
Canal bank and canal bridge are both natural scenes.
River bank is a compound and bridges cross rivers.

best_available.why: The broadest shared scene for the two words.

pairs.pair_note: RIVER is the obvious winner; CANAL is a valid variant of the same scene.

hints.reason: Castle moat is immediate, but a moat having banks (or the finance sense of 'moat') is a stretch.
The castle keep is a set term, and a bank keeps your money, but the BANK side is a verb pun rather than a recognizable phrase.
Treasury is core bank vocabulary and castles have a treasury room where the royal hoard is kept.

best_available.why: Finance word that also names a familiar castle room.

pairs.pair_note: TREASURY is a fair PASS; KEEP is a pleasant pun that may deserve a second look.

hints.reason: Cat whiskers only; nothing for BANK.
Cat burglar is a set phrase and burglars rob banks.

best_available.why: Compound on the CAT side, obvious crime scene on the BANK side.

pairs.pair_note: BURGLAR is strong; WHISKERS is filler.

hints.reason: Gold is kept in bank vaults and crowns are made of gold.
A sovereign wears the crown, and sovereign is a gold coin / sovereign debt in bank vocabulary.
A mint makes the money banks hold, but CROWN is reached only via the Royal Mint or crown-stamped coins.
Royal Bank (of Scotland, of Canada) is a familiar brand and crowns are royal.

best_available.why: The most immediate shared material.

pairs.pair_note: A rich pair; GOLD and ROYAL are both strong, SOVEREIGN is clever but skews British.

hints.reason: Bank robber is a compound, but DOG is reached only through dogs chasing or catching robbers.
Guard dog is a compound and bank guard is a familiar job.

best_available.why: Equally direct on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: GUARD is a model hint; ROBBER is a bank hint with a dog-shaped afterthought.

hints.reason: Banks hold gold and dragons sleep on gold.
A dragon's hoard is the set phrase and hoarding money in a bank is a recognizable idea.
Dragon fire only; no ordinary route to BANK.

best_available.why: The shared treasure image is immediate.

pairs.pair_note: GOLD and HOARD both work; FIRE is filler.

hints.reason: Egg yolk only; nothing for BANK.
Nest egg is the set phrase for savings kept in the bank; the EGG side is literal.

best_available.why: Nest egg is the one phrase that ties eggs to savings.

pairs.pair_note: NEST is a fair PASS on the strength of 'nest egg'; YOLK is filler.

hints.reason: Break the bank and firebreak are both set phrases.
Fire alarm is a compound and bank alarms go off in robberies.
Bank safe and fire safe (fireproof safe) are both familiar objects.

best_available.why: A single object that is literally a bank safe and a fire safe.

pairs.pair_note: All three pass; SAFE is the tightest.

hints.reason: Fish fin is immediate, but BANK is reached only via 'fin' as slang for a five-dollar bill or as a finance abbreviation.
River bank is a compound and river fish is an everyday scene.

best_available.why: The shared scene is instant.

pairs.pair_note: RIVER is strong; FIN is a slang stretch.

hints.reason: Ghosts vanish, but money vanishing from a bank is a mood rather than a phrase.
Bank account is a compound and a ghost account (abandoned or fake account) is a reasonably familiar phrase.
Ghost town is a compound, but BANK is reached only as a building every town has.
The bedsheet ghost is immediate, but BANK is reached only through a balance sheet.
Bank vault is a compound, but GHOST is reached only through a burial vault or crypt.

best_available.why: The only hint where both sides are set phrases, even if 'ghost account' is less universal.

pairs.pair_note: A hard pair; ACCOUNT is a modest PASS and worth a second opinion, the rest are each one-sided in a different direction.

hints.reason: Bank vault only; GLASS has no ordinary vault connection.
The teller window at a bank and the glass in a window are both immediate.

best_available.why: Direct on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: WINDOW carries the pair; VAULT is filler here.

hints.reason: Gold bar is a compound, but BANK is reached only through the bars gold comes in or bars on a vault.
Bank vault is a compound and gold is what sits in it.
Federal Reserve bank and gold reserve are both set phrases.

best_available.why: The shared object is immediate.

pairs.pair_note: VAULT and RESERVE both pass comfortably; BAR is nearly there but one-sided.

hints.reason: Robbing a bank is immediate, but HONEY is reached only via bears robbing hives or the beekeeping sense of robbing.
Honey pot is a compound, but BANK is reached only as a pot of money.
Banks store money and bees store honey; the shared verb reaches both sides clearly.

best_available.why: The one hint whose route is equally clear on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: STORE is generic but fair; ROB and POT each lean on one word.

hints.reason: River bank is a compound and a frozen river is a familiar image.
A frozen bank account and frozen ice are both immediate.

best_available.why: A finance phrase that is also the defining property of ice.

pairs.pair_note: FROZEN is excellent; RIVER is a fair second.

hints.reason: A king's crown is immediate, but BANK is reached only through the crown as a coin or the Crown as the state.
Royal Bank brands on one side and a royal king on the other.
Kings are rich and a full bank account is what makes you rich; broad but it reaches both.

best_available.why: A brand route on the BANK side keeps it concrete.

pairs.pair_note: ROYAL is strong; RICH is a modest PASS; CROWN is mostly a king hint.

hints.reason: A knight's armor is immediate and the armored truck that carries bank cash is a recognizable scene.
A bank charge (fee) and a knight's charge are both ordinary uses.

best_available.why: Clean double meaning, each side ordinary.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass; CHARGE is the tighter one.

hints.reason: Street light is a compound and Wall Street / the high-street bank put banks on the street.
Green light is a compound, but BANK is reached only through green as the colour of money.
Light switch is a compound, but switching banks is a thin verb route.
Floodlight is a compound and a river in flood overflows its banks.

best_available.why: Compound on one side and a familiar river-bank scene on the other.

pairs.pair_note: FLOOD is the best; STREET is a fair PASS; GREEN and SWITCH each lean on LIGHT.

hints.reason: Lions roar; nothing for BANK.
Stone lions guarding the steps of a grand bank is a recognizable shared scene, and lion statues are common in their own right.

best_available.why: The lion-statue-outside-the-bank scene reaches both words.

pairs.pair_note: STATUE is a fair PASS on the strength of the classic bank facade; ROAR is filler.

hints.reason: A silver moon is immediate and silver is the precious metal banks hold alongside gold.
River bank is a compound and Moon River / moonlight on a river is a familiar image.
The moon belongs to night, but BANK is reached only via the night-deposit slot.

best_available.why: The metal route to BANK is a notch below GOLD but still recognizable.

pairs.pair_note: Two fair passes; neither is as tight as the best hints elsewhere.

hints.reason: Mouse and cheese only; nothing for BANK.
Online banking on one side and the computer mouse you do it with on the other.

best_available.why: A clean modern scene that needs both words.

pairs.pair_note: ONLINE is strong; CHEESE is filler.

hints.reason: Dark is near-synonymous with night and has no ordinary route to BANK.
Bank deposit is a compound and the night deposit slot is the one place NIGHT meets banking.

best_available.why: Night deposit is the single phrase joining the two words.

pairs.pair_note: DEPOSIT passes because both sides are set phrases; DARK is filler.

hints.reason: Ocean wave only; WAVE has no ordinary route to BANK.
Sandbank is a compound and sand is the ocean shore.

best_available.why: Compound on one side, defining scene on the other.

pairs.pair_note: SAND is strong; WAVE is filler.

hints.reason: Pirate's parrot only; nothing for BANK.
Pirate loot is a set phrase and bank robbers make off with loot.
Robbing a bank and pirates robbing ships are both immediate.

best_available.why: The noun reads as a shared object rather than a shared verb.

pairs.pair_note: LOOT and ROB are both good and near-duplicates; PARROT is filler.

hints.reason: Queen bee only; nothing for BANK.
Bank of England and Queen of England are both set phrases.

best_available.why: Parallel 'X of England' phrases on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: ENGLAND is excellent; BEE is filler.

hints.reason: Diamond ring is a compound, but BANK is reached only as a place diamonds might be stored.
A bank safe or safe-deposit box is immediate, and keeping a ring in the safe is a recognizable scene.

best_available.why: The ring-in-the-safe scene joins both words.

pairs.pair_note: SAFE is a fair PASS; DIAMOND is mostly a ring hint.

hints.reason: Robot arm is immediate, but BANK is reached only via ARM as an adjustable-rate mortgage, which no player will see.
A bank ATM is immediate and the automated teller is machine-like, but ROBOT is implied rather than recognized.

best_available.why: The automated-machine idea is the only real bridge offered to ROBOT.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. ATM as a robot teller is a defensible stretch and worth a second opinion; ARM fails.

hints.reason: River bank and river rocks are the same scene.
Rock solid is a set phrase, but a 'solid bank' is marketing language rather than a recognized route.

best_available.why: Instant shared scene.

pairs.pair_note: RIVER is strong; SOLID leans on ROCK.

hints.reason: A river bursting its banks is a set phrase, but a rose bursting into bloom is a loose verb association.
Rose bed is a compound, but BANK is reached only as the river bed's neighbour.
Hedge fund is finance vocabulary and a rose hedge is an ordinary garden feature.

best_available.why: A finance word that is also a literal rose planting.

pairs.pair_note: HEDGE carries the pair; BURST and BED each lean on one side.

hints.reason: Net worth is bank vocabulary and 'worth one's salt' is a familiar idiom.
Bank deposit and salt deposit are both compounds.
Salary is paid into the bank, and the salt-to-salary etymology is well-known trivia even if not universal.

best_available.why: Both sides are literal compounds.

pairs.pair_note: A rich pair; SALARY is the only hint that depends on a fact rather than a phrase.

hints.reason: Cloud bank is a compound and clouds cast shadows.
Shade is a near-synonym of shadow and has no route to BANK.

best_available.why: Compound on the BANK side, physical fact on the SHADOW side.

pairs.pair_note: CLOUD is a good hint; SHADE is a synonym of one target.
